chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father:
"That when he prayed alone in the house, he would establish the Iqamah and not give the Adhan."

key_terms.إِقَامَة: Iqamah (the second call to prayer, recited immediately before standing for prayer)
key_terms.الْبَيْت: The house (referring to a private residence)
key_terms.صَلَّى وَحْدَهُ: Prayed alone (individual prayer, as opposed to congregational prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on giving Adhan and Iqamah when praying alone at home according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic distinction between the Adhan and Iqamah based on location and congregation size, establishing that the Adhan is primarily a public announcement while the Iqamah serves as the immediate signal to commence prayer. By omitting the Adhan when praying alone indoors, the Imam (peace be upon him) demonstrated the practical application of *sunnah* regarding the removal of unnecessary ritual elements, a principle often cited by Shia jurists when deriving rulings for private worship.
